LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we write legibly and neatly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify text written in joined letters or cursive script
2. write legibly using joined letters/cursive script

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 3.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: HANDWRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 3.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: HANDWRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify text written in joined letters or cursive script

What this means
In this part you learn to identify text written in joined letters or cursive script. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify text written in joined letters or cursive script.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify text written in joined letters or cursive script. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write legibly using joined letters/cursive script

What this means
In this part you learn to write legibly using joined letters/cursive script. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write legibly using joined letters/cursive script.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write legibly using joined letters/cursive script. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify text written in joined letters or cursive script)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting to a partner. (skill: write legibly using joined letters/cursive script)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify text written in joined letters or cursive script.
3. Practise this skill: write legibly using joined letters/cursive script.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we write legibly and neatly?
2. How can you improve your handwriting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 3.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Handwriting means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify text written in joined letters or cursive script.
5. Be able to: write legibly using joined letters/cursive script.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
